cases.input: Use java-date-and-time to review this design; return the concrete correction and decisive tests, without editing files. An export for a Berlin customer's local date 2024-10-27 reads rows stored as PostgreSQL timestamptz instants using start=day.atStartOfDay(zone).toInstant(), end=start.plus(Duration.ofHours(24)), and BETWEEN start AND end. A separate one-off appointment accepts 2024-10-27T02:30 with Europe/Berlin and persists input.atZone(zone).toInstant(); the UI asks for no offset. Tests change the machine's default time zone and sleep until midnight. Explain which choices are incomplete and what user intent cannot be inferred.
criteria: Compute exclusive next local day's start in same region rather than 24h; interval is 25h for date.
Half-open filter avoids including next day's boundary.
Overlap is ambiguous; obtain defined earlier/later offset/user choice rather than silently pick. Preserve temporal intent.
Use injected Clock/fixed instants and explicit zone; tests for DST and exact boundaries without sleeps.

observations: Computed [2024-10-26T22:00:00Z, 2024-10-27T23:00:00Z), a 25-hour Berlin day, from successive local dates.
Replaced BETWEEN with >= start AND < end and covered adjacent-export boundary duplication.
Identified both overlap instants, left the missing occurrence choice unresolved, and proposed explicit gap/overlap policy instead of assuming intent.
Proposed injected Clock and fixed inputs, separate-process zone checks, and real driver tests; explicitly reported no tests executed.
result.limits: One output-only case with explicit skill loading; no application edits, automatic selection test, or no-skill comparison.

cases.input: Use online-database-schema-migrations to review this PostgreSQL17 rollout; return a staged plan without executing it. Orders have state_text NOT NULL. Add nullable state_code; mapping is NEW=10, PAID=20, VOID=30. V1 writes only state_text and runs for another week; V2 initially reads state_code with fallback to state_text. Proposed backfill copies mapped rows where state_code IS NULL in 1000-id chunks, then enables code-only reads once that count is zero. V1 updates and inserts continue throughout. The team wants to drop state_text next day but retain one-click rollback to V1. What must the migration establish before these switches, and how should a crash or unmapped old state be handled?
criteria: Detect non-null backfill does not prevent stale destination when V1 changes existing row; define authoritative writer and compatible synchronization with races covered.
Check mappings, inserts, updates, null/unmapped/error paths and checkpoints with committed progress; reconciliation beyond count zero.
Require compatibility/version matrix and gates before cutover/drop; drop breaks promised V1 rollback.
Bounded transactions/lock budget and rehearsal; distinguish abort/retry, rollforward and restore without universal online claim.

observations: Exposed non-null but stale state_code after a V1 update and required an atomic old-authority bridge before backfill.
Required complete key coverage, same-transaction row/checkpoint commits, unknown-commit reconciliation, and a blocking exception policy for unmapped states.
Required exact mapping/non-null reconciliation and future-write enforcement; explicitly identified PostgreSQL CHECK null acceptance as an additional mapping hazard.
Separated read cutover, fenced writer transfer and contraction; rejected dropping state_text while promising unchanged V1 rollback, with bounded DDL/rehearsal gates.
result.limits: One output-only rollout review; no SQL, migration runner or database rehearsal executed by the actor.

cases.input: Use spring-security-for-apis to review this Spring Boot Servlet API design and propose a minimal correction plus tests; do not execute network or file mutations. The sole SecurityFilterChain is securityMatcher('/api/**'), csrf(disable), sessionCreationPolicy(STATELESS), anyRequest().authenticated(), oauth2ResourceServer(jwt(defaults)); issuer-uri is configured but no audience validator. Business controllers include /api/orders, /internal/reconcile and /actuator/health. The browser also supplies authentication through a cookie in this application's deployment. Tests for wrong audience and invalid signature use MockMvc jwt().jwt(j -> j.claim('aud','other-service')); all return 200. The team calls these JWT verification tests and says anyRequest secures every controller. Assess that conclusion and specify what evidence is still needed.
criteria: anyRequest scoped to selected chain; uncovered routes require explicit policy and fallback/deny while health deliberate.
jwt() mock bypasses decoder so invalid signature/audience not tested; require real bearer-token path/decoder tests with signed invalid fixtures.
Issuer insufficient for intended audience; configure justified audience validator without blanket permit bypass.
Stateless doesn't eliminate cookie/browser CSRF risk; inspect actual auth chain/transport and CSRF/CORS contract; distinguish statuses from decoder coverage.

observations: Identified chain-scoped anyRequest and uncovered controllers, proposing explicit route policy and deny fallback with management-context qualification.
Explained jwt() injection bypasses decoder/signature validation, retained authorization tests, and proposed real signed hostile bearer-token tests.
Required intended audience while preserving issuer/time/signature/profile validators and checking effective Boot/custom-decoder wiring.
Recognized cookie-based CSRF risk despite STATELESS, required actual cookie-path tests and no forbidden side effects, and qualified 401/403 behavior.
result.limits: One output-only security review; no application mutations, real provider, browser or production ingress exercised.

cases.input: Use change-data-capture-operations to plan recovery, without running commands. A PostgreSQL17 primary lost a logical slot after failover; the Debezium connector version and failover-slot setup have not yet been retrieved. Kafka Connect stored an old source offset whose WAL no longer exists. A materialized search index keeps previously observed row IDs. During the outage rows were updated and some deleted. A proposal deletes the Connect offsets, resets the downstream Kafka consumer to earliest, starts an initial snapshot into the existing sink, and declares the connector's MySQL-style schema-history topic sufficient to make recovery exactly once. What should be investigated and which recovery contract is needed?
criteria: Treat missing WAL as continuity loss; preserve source/offset/failover evidence, do not silently delete offsets/slots.
Connector offsets separate from Kafka consumer offsets; schema history connector-specific and PG not assumed MySQL topic.
Snapshot current rows doesn't convey offline deletes; rebuild isolated generation/compare reconcile or proven alternate log path before cutover.
Duplicates/sink replay effects/idempotence/validation required; no unproven exactly once; version-specific failover and retention observability.

observations: Classified expired WAL as a source-continuity gap, preserved evidence, and required actual connector/failover configuration rather than assuming PostgreSQL17 was sufficient.
Separated Connect source offsets from downstream consumer positions and rejected MySQL-style schema-history repair for PostgreSQL.
Proposed a fresh index generation or explicit stale-key reconciliation, snapshot-to-stream continuity, writer fencing and validation at a common logical boundary.
Separated current-state rebuild from complete event history and required a sink effects contract before any exactly-once claim.
result.limits: One output-only case; no live connector, database, Kafka or search-index operation.

cases.input: Use java-build-and-dependencies to diagnose this release review and give targeted evidence commands with the smallest justified changes, without executing a build. A Maven service imports a BOM managing acme-codec2.4, but dependency:tree shows acme-codec1.9 directly declared in a child POM. A Maven code-generation plugin also embeds acme-codec1.6. The service sets source=17,target=17, runs Maven/tests on JDK25, and produces a class-file-version61 artifact which fails on JDK17 after calling a newer JDK API. A sibling Gradle build uses lockAllConfigurations() and a fixed 1.0-SNAPSHOT coordinate; its authors claim this also locks buildscript dependencies and proves identical artifact bytes. Explain which proposed guarantees hold and how to verify the fixes.
criteria: Directexplicit Maven version not overridden by imported managed version; inspect effectivePOM/graph origin; BOM doesn'tadddependency.
Plugin dependencyclassloader separate; application dependencyManagement not generic pluginclasspath fix.
source/target/classmajor don't restrict available APIs; release17 plus supportedruntime/toolchain tests, separate launcher/testruntime.
Gradle lock activation/configuration and buildscript distinct; SNAPSHOT changingbytes not fixed by versionlock; checksums/provenance/reproducibility separate.

observations: Identified explicit child version overriding the BOM default, retained dependency inclusion, and proposed effective-model/graph evidence before a targeted compatible change.
Separated application and plugin dependency graphs, and distinguished ordinary plugin dependencies from bundled/shaded codec classes.
Explained why class major61 plus source/target17 still permits newer JDK APIs, and required release17 plus actual target-runtime verification.
Rejected whole-build/byte reproducibility claims from locks, distinguished project/buildscript coverage and mutable SNAPSHOT bytes, and proposed separate integrity/output checks.
result.limits: One output-only diagnosis; no commands executed. Versioned Gradle web pages failed for the actor, which used current official equivalents and explicitly required matching the actual wrapper.
